name: IS corpus (Query file manager)
blurb: The India standards corpus — IS 800, IS 801, IS 811, IS 808, IS 1161, IS 2062, IS 875 (Parts 1–5), IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 + Amd 1/2, IS 18168:2023 and the connection standards — converted from licensed BIS PDFs, with the full-text / exact-id search the design agents ground their clauses on. PRIVATE repository: Install clones it with this PC's own GitHub credentials, or link a working copy on disk. No vector DB; nothing leaves this PC.

converter.label: PDF converter (Docling 2.123.1)
converter.help: Only needed to convert a BIS PDF you licensed yourself (the corpus repo already carries the converted documents). Large download (ML stack). The corpus pins 2.123.1 — do not upgrade without revalidating retrieval accuracy. The [rapidocr] extra adds onnxruntime, which convert_pdf.py's RapidOCR fallback needs on the scanned BIS prints (IS 801, IS 811, IS 816, IS 875-5).

tabs.title: Corpus
tabs.blurb: What this machine actually has: the converted BIS documents, their edition, collection name and quality grade (PASS / REPAIRED / DEGRADED with the known defects from the corpus README), and the FTS index. Run this first.

run.label: Check corpus

tabs.title: Query
tabs.blurb: Verbatim excerpts from the converted BIS documents. `found: false` is an honest answer — nothing is paraphrased or invented; a US term (SDS, Cd, Ω0 …) answers found:false with the IS equivalent, and a town in neither IS 875-3 Annex A nor IS 1893 Annex E answers not_tabulated (read the map). Every hit is standard text (BIS documents carry no separate commentary); always verify numbers against the PDF page the hit names — formula text from OCR / Docling can be garbled, and a hand-typed Canonical line follows the clause where it matters.

fields.label: Project
fields.help: Queries are logged to this project's folder.

options.label: Table id (or a section designation: HB 300, MC 175)

fields.label: Query
fields.placeholder: e.g. 7.1.2   ·   Table 9   ·   basic wind speed Chennai   ·   HB 300   ·   importance factor hospital

fields.label: Document
fields.help: Canonical stems, fixed by the corpus (retrieval ids depend on them). A collection name (engineering_standards_IS800) is accepted too.

options.label: IS 875 (Part 4):2021 snow (stem keeps its historical name)

fields.label: Include commentary (none in BIS documents — kept for parity)
fields.help: BIS documents carry no separate commentary volume: every India hit is part=standard. Off by default.

tabs.title: Convert PDF
tabs.blurb: Convert a BIS PDF you licensed yourself with Docling at full accuracy (TableFormer ACCURATE, formula enrichment on, OCR fallback for scanned prints), post-processed with the is_bis profile. Only needed for a document the corpus repo does not already carry, or to re-convert one from your own copy; the output lands in documents/standards/<STEM>. Needs the optional component "PDF converter (Docling 2.123.1)" — install it once from the Modules tab (large download, the ML stack); the hub refuses to run this tab until it is present. Then run Rebuild index and Validate corpus. The licence watermark of BIS PDFs is stripped by the post-processing (strip_watermark.py --check reports what remains).

run.label: Convert
run.crash_hint: Convert again with the same stem -- it resumes from the last finished chunk (the log shows 'Resume: reusing existing chunk pages'). If it dies at the same place twice, lower Pages per chunk (5 -> 2) or use Page range to isolate the page; a memory-hungry page in PyTorch or onnxruntime is the usual cause.

fields.label: Specification PDF
fields.help: Your own licensed BIS copy. Nothing is uploaded anywhere — conversion runs on this machine.

fields.label: Canonical stem
fields.help: Must match exactly: the retrieval ids and the collection map (engineering_standards_IS*) are keyed on these stems.

options.label: IS 875 (Part 4):2021 snow (stem keeps its historical name)

fields.label: Pages per chunk
fields.help: 5 is the documented default. Lower it only to work around out-of-memory, never to gain speed.

tabs.title: Re-process
tabs.blurb: Rebuild one converted document's searchable markdown, sections, equations and tables from the Docling chunks already on disk — no re-conversion, minutes not hours. Use it after a pipeline fix, or when a document's text looks like another's. Pick the stem, and give it the source PDF if you have it (equation ids, table captions and ligature repair all read it), then run Rebuild index.

run.label: Re-process document
run.crash_hint: Re-processing reads the PDF only for the equation census; if it died there, run it again with the source PDF left blank.

fields.label: Converted document
fields.help: The converted document's folder under documents/standards (the Corpus tab lists them).

options.label: IS 875 (Part 4):2021 snow (stem keeps its historical name)

fields.label: Source PDF (optional)
fields.help: Only needed for the equation census. Leave empty to skip it.

tabs.title: Rebuild index
tabs.blurb: Rebuild the unified indexes (sections, tables, equations, documents with edition and quality) and the FTS index after converting or revising documents: per-document BIS index repair, then the unified build. Follow it with Validate corpus.

tabs.title: Validate corpus
tabs.blurb: The corpus's must-hit probes (validate.py --corpus): clause, table and section-row lookups that must answer (IS 1893 Table 9 Note 1, IS 800 7.1.2.1, IS 808 HB 300, the town annexes, IS 18168 5.5), the US-term trap, and a grep that no licence watermark line survives in any text artefact. Exit 1 = the build is not usable. Rebuild index first.

tabs.title: Retrieval plan
tabs.blurb: Run a whole retrieval plan at once — the batch path an agent uses to fill a load_plan or nl_plan from many clause queries (serve_queue.py --plan).

fields.label: Plan JSON
fields.help: {plan_id, submitted, queries:[{qid, doc, type, query, purpose, want_commentary, context_neighbors}]}

tabs.title: Grounding
tabs.blurb: What the design agents are asking this corpus, and what they got back. HR Steel (IS 800) and CFS (IS 801) point their standards search here automatically (RAG_API_URL).
